title: The FOMC Announcement Reversal
one_line: On scheduled FOMC days, the S&P 500 reverses the prior 24 hours: buying E-mini at 13:50 ET after a negative prior-24h return (selling after a positive one) and exiting at the close earned ~0.18% per announcement net of spreads, Sharpe ≈ 0.36 (180 announcements, Oct 1997-Jan 2020).

findings.statement: Rule: sign = −sign(prior 24h return), enter 13:50 ET (10 min before the release), exit at the day's close; buys at ask / sells at bid.

findings.evidence: Subperiods 1997-2011 and 2011-2020 studied; varies with VIX and policy uncertainty (details behind paywall).

why.pattern: Pre-announcement positioning (and the pre-FOMC drift) unwinds once the decision resolves uncertainty.

reported_results.headline: On scheduled FOMC days, the S&P 500 reverses the prior 24 hours: buying E-mini at 13:50 ET after a negative prior-24h return (selling after a positive one) and exiting at the close earned ~0.18% per announcement net of spreads, Sharpe ≈ 0.36 (180 announcements, Oct 1997-Jan 2020).

tradable_edge: New spec fomc_announcement_reversal_es — fully testable on ES/NQ 1-min with the public FOMC calendar.

decay_risk.reason: ≈ 8 trades/yr; few observations, but our 2014-2023 window is mostly out of sample.

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
